subject: CrestPoint: ephemeral log timeline, deletion evidence and exception request

Subject: Info request: ephemeral logs, deletion timeline & evidence

Hi Neha,

We're doing a quick SIG + CAIQ deep-dive ahead of our pilot kickoff next week. Two items on the list where your team helps:

1) Concrete evidence of the ephemeral logging timeline for inference kernels / GPU nodes and any aggregated logs retained centrally (we need the retention windows and the deletion process).
2) What artifacts you can share that show deletion occurred (hashes, snapshots, log export, or runbook excerpts).

Specifically, crestpoint's security posture requires confirmation that raw inference node logs are not retained past X days (we expect a short window) and that any longer-term traces are aggregated and scrubbed of prompt text unless a customer opts-in.

Can you provide:
- A short runbook excerpt or ticket showing a deletion job for ephemeral logs (PDF or CSV stub is fine)
- A sample syslog export (anonymized) showing timestamps and retention metadata
- Clarification on whether prompt/response text ever flows into long-term ELK or S3 exports by default

If a customer requests a retention exception (e.g., retain for 180 days for a regulated pilot), what's the process, approvals, and technical controls we would need? Also: estimated cost/impact.

Attaching a one-page checklist of the SIG questions we need answered.

Thanks,
Samir Kapoor
Security Lead, CrestPoint Financial
[sent from phone]

Attachments: crestpoint-sig-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Info request: ephemeral logs, deletion timeline & evidence

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (product) and Kimberly (security/forensics) to pull the artifacts and confirm the process. Quick answers up-front:

- Default ephemeral log retention (node-level): 7 days. These are on ephemeral local volumes attached to GPU nodes; they are rotated and deleted automatically by the node reclaim process.
- Aggregated telemetry (agent/metrics/alerts) shipped to central logging cluster: retained 90 days by default.
- Long-term S3 bucket exports (for audits/backups): retained 30 days unless a customer-specific contract extends that.
- Prompt/response text: by default, prompt outputs are not persisted into long-term ELK exports. We store request/response artifacts only when a customer explicitly enables request tracing for debugging or opts into log archiving — otherwise we keep only metadata (request id, latency, error codes, hashes).

What we'll provide this week:
- A redacted syslog sample from an ephemeral node (tar.gz stub)
- Our retention matrix CSV (redwood-retention-matrix.csv) with TTLs and deletion mechanisms
- A short excerpt from the internal forensics runbook describing the deletion job and evidence artifacts (forensics-runbook-sample.pdf)

Two clarifying Qs so we meet your evidence bar:
1) For the deletion proof do you prefer a) a timestamped job log + file inventory, b) hash+deletion-record pair, or c) an exported ticket from our internal job scheduler showing the run and exit code? We can provide any combination.
2) Is the pilot request you mentioned specifically asking that raw prompts be retained for 180 days, or just aggregated telemetry expanded to 180 days?

We can also schedule a short 30-minute call with Kimberly to walk through the artifacts and the legal hold workflow if that helps.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Security
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir@crestpoint.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Info request: ephemeral logs, deletion timeline & evidence

Hi all — technical detail below and what I attached. High-level summary first: we have a 3-layer retention model (ephemeral node -> central logging -> optional S3 export).

1) Ephemeral node logs- Location: local ephemeral volume on worker node (/var/log/redwood/worker-*)- TTL: 7 days by automated rotation + node-reclaim deletion- Evidence artifacts: job run log from our node lifecycle controller and file inventory snapshot taken immediately prior to deletion. We can provide a zipped sample of the inventory CSV and job stdout (redacted).

2) Central logging cluster (ELK)
- Ingest: logs are forwarded via secured agent over mTLS- Default retention: 90 days (indices rolled daily)- Prompt data: we explicitly strip user prompt/response payloads at ingest unless tracing is enabled by customer. Tracing is opt-in and gated by a signed configuration change per customer.- Evidence artifacts: index snapshot manifest (index name, creation time, doc counts) and delete-by-query job logs when we remove data. We keep an audit trail in our metastore that shows index deletion timestamps.

3) S3 exports (audit/backups)
- Purpose: occasional exports for audits / support; default retention 30 days; immutable copies can be kept longer under contract- Controls: objects encrypted with KMS (customer and/or Redwood keys).

Legal hold / customer-specific exception flow:
- Customer submits formal request to legal (legal@crestpoint.io) and CCs Redwood security (kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com).
- We create a scoped request in our change control system; legal approves and we create a configuration pin for that customer.
- Technical implementation: enable tracing/archival flag for the customer's tenant which routes additional artifacts to a dedicated long-term bucket. We mark those buckets as non-auto-delete and apply retention per contract.
- Approval windows: Security + Legal sign-off; operational lead schedules the migration (can take 24–72 hours depending on shard sizes).

Impact and cost considerations (ballpark):
- Storage cost: if you keep full request/response payloads for 180 days expect ~3x–10x uplift depending on request size and sampling.
- Forensic retrieval time: snapshot/extract ops could add 4–12 hours for large datasets; SLA for access depends on the export size.

Attachments included:
- redwood-retention-matrix.csv (CSV) — TTLs and target locations- forensics-runbook-sample.pdf (PDF excerpt)- crestpoint-syslog-sample.tar.gz (redacted sample)

If you want cryptographic deletion evidence, we can provide a hash+deletion-record pair from the job output; we do not currently provide signed certificates for each deletion as an automated product feature, but we can produce attestations on request (legal-approved).

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Security & Forensics, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that's helpful and closer to what we need. A couple quick follow-ups:

1) For the pilot we are exploring a retention exception to keep full request/response artifacts for 180 days for a scoped customer cohort (10 tenants) for fraud analysis. We understand the cost implications; please put together two options: a) keep full artifacts for 180d with estimated storage delta and retrieval SLA; b) keep only metadata + sampled payloads (1% sample) for 180d with estimated delta.
2) We need to confirm that the exported artifacts (if enabled) include the full prompt/response content unredacted — and whether Redwood can apply on-export redaction rules (e.g., PII masking) prior to long-term storage.

Can you add a short note on the estimated lead time to enable the exception (from legal sign-off to data actually being retained) and a high-level cost estimate? If you prefer, we'll take the deeper pricing discussion to a follow-up call.

Appreciate the quick turn.

Samir
Security Lead, CrestPoint Financial
